rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet commends joining gentleness with firmness and likens striking without remedy to an injury without a surgeon or balm.
rows.anchor: درشتى ونرمى بهم در بهست ورك زن كه جراح ومرهم نهست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is told to speak gently to Pharaoh, despite his disbelief, out of regard for the right of the man who raised him; this signals the respect owed to parents.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أمر الله موسى باللين مع الكافر مراعاة لحق التربية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: As transmitted in al-Iḥyāʾ, al-Hasan says a child may admonish a father while he is calm but should fall silent when the father becomes angry.
rows.anchor: وفي الإحياء سئل الحسن عن الولد كيف يحتسب على والده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child must not rebuke or strike a parent harshly; a student differs, since a scholar who does not practice his knowledge has no such inviolability.
rows.anchor: فعلم منه أنه ليس للولد الحسبة على الوالد بالتعنيف والضرب وليس كذلك التلميذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gentleness leaves Pharaoh no excuse to claim that Moses used harsh words in calling him to faith.
rows.anchor: وقيل أمر موسى باللين ليكون حجة على فرعون لئلا يقول أغلظ علي القول

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Muʿadh wept, marveling that God treats gently even someone who claims to be God, and asking how much greater His gentleness is toward one who acknowledges Him.
rows.anchor: قرأ رجل عند يحيى بن معاذ رحمه الله هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshād says Pharaoh may remember the reminder and desire what the brothers urge, or fear God's punishment; or does not exclude either outcome.
rows.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" لعله يتذكر بما بلغتماه من ذكري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say hope and expectation describe Moses and Aaron, remembrance concerns what is established, and fear what is supposed; fear is awe mixed with reverence and commonly arises from knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الرجاء والطمع راجعان إلى مال موسى وهارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of fear as especially associated with the learned is linked to the statement that only the learned truly fear God.
rows.anchor: ولذلك خص العلماء بها في قوله {ومن الناس والدوآب والانعام مختلف ألوانه}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers hope Pharaoh will stop denying truth: he might accept wholeheartedly after reflection, or at least suspect it is true and fear persisting in denial; either is better than stubborn rejection.
rows.anchor: راجيين أن يترك الإصرار على إنكار الحق وتكذيبه إما بأن يتذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh remembered and feared only when drowning, when that response could no longer benefit him.
rows.anchor: ولقد تذكر فرعون وخشي حين لم ينفعاه وذلك حين ألجمه الغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses promised Pharaoh lasting youth, rule until death, worldly pleasures until death, and Paradise afterward if he believed; Haman persuaded him that accepting would make a supposed god subject to another, so he refused.
rows.anchor: روي أن موسى وعده على قبول الإيمان شبابا لا يهرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending the messengers despite God's knowledge that Pharaoh will not believe establishes proof and removes his excuse; God's custom is to deliver the message before punishment.
rows.anchor: وفائدة إرسالهما إليه مع علمه تعالى بأنه لا يؤمن الزام الحجة

rows.speaker: بعض أرباب الحقيقة
rows.claim: Some people of spiritual realization distinguish God's prescriptive command from His decree: messengers and heirs serve the prescriptive command, although it may differ from what God decrees.
rows.anchor: قال بعض أرباب الحقيقة : الأمر تكليفي وإرادي والإرادة كثيرا ما تكون مخالفة للأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sinner's fixed identity in divine knowledge has capacity for the duty but no readiness to perform it, which explains disobedience.
rows.anchor: العاصي الثابتة في الحضرة العلمية استعداد التكليف توجه إليه الأمر التكليفي وليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point of a command known not to be fulfilled is to distinguish those ready to accept from those not ready, making felicity and misery manifest.
rows.anchor: قلت : فائدته تمييز من له استعداد القبول ممن ليس له استعداد ذلك

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafez's couplet expresses surrender to one's divinely directed course rather than self-reproach.
rows.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
جزء : 5 رقم الصفحة : 388
درين من مكنم سرزنش بخود

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr says God's knowledge follows what is known as it is; knowing that Pharaoh freely chooses disbelief does not make belief impossible, so God still commands the two to call him gently.
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" : إن الله قد علم كل شيء على ما هو عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī takes the verse's hope of remembrance or fear as evidence that human capacity affects one's own and others' acts, rejecting al-Ashʿarī's view that people are compelled and their capacity has no effect.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : {لعله يتذكر أو يخشى} دلالة ظاهرة على أن لقدرة العبد تأثيرا

rows.speaker: الأشعري
rows.claim: Al-Ashʿarī is cited as denying any effect of human capacity on acts and describing humans as compelled; Bursevī argues the verse contradicts this.
rows.anchor: كما زعم الأشعري حيث قال لا تأثير لقدرة العبد في أفعاله بل هو مجبور

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshād says the plural speech is by grammatical predominance: Moses is primary in every word and deed, while Aaron follows him.
rows.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" أسند القول إليهما مع أن القائل حقيقة هو موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses traveled from the mountain toward Egypt alone, without knowing the route and without provisions, mount, or companion; he lived on sparse fruit and game until reaching Egypt.
rows.anchor: وروي أن موسى انطلق من الطور إلى جانب مصر لا علم له بالطريق

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kāshifī says revelation sent Aaron to meet Moses on the road; after hearing the story, Aaron warned of Pharaoh's power and readiness to kill or crucify, making the brothers apprehensive and prayerful.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ون بمصر توجه فرمود وحى آمد بهارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear expects harm based on a likely or known sign, unlike hope, which expects something desired; fear contrasts with security and applies to worldly and next-worldly matters.
rows.anchor: الخوف توقع مكروه عن إمارة مظنونة أو معلومة كما أن الرجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of God here means restraining oneself from sins and choosing obedience, rather than bodily terror before a lion.
rows.anchor: والخوف من الله يراد به ما يخطر بالبال من الرعب كاستشعار الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb derives from going ahead; a farit prepares a water vessel, so the phrase means Pharaoh may hasten to punish them before the mission and sign are complete.
rows.anchor: من فرط إذا تقدم تقدما بالقصد ومنه الفارط إلى الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading derives the verb from ifrāṭ, meaning excess in causing harm.
rows.anchor: وقرىء يفرط من الإفراط في الأذية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says fear is rooted in human nature even in prophets; Moses and Aaron fear not death itself but failing in servitude by being prevented from delivering the message, while Pharaoh may rebel and insult God's commands.
rows.anchor: كما في "التأويلات النجمية" يشير إلى أن الخوف مركوز في جبلة الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh may grow tyrannical and say what is unfitting about God; the wording courteously says in God's regard rather than against Him, and leaves the greater offense to the end.
rows.anchor: أي : يزداد طغيانا إلى أن يقول في شأنك ما لا ينبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī also allows that Pharaoh may tyrannize against Moses and Aaron; the preposition is omitted for the verse ending, as the object is omitted in another verse for cadence.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : يجوز أن يكون المراد يطغى علينا أي : يجاوز الحد في الإساءة إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb قال begins an explanatory answer to the implied question of what God said in response to their plea.
rows.anchor: {قال} استئناف بياني كأنه قيل فماذا قال لهما ربهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not fear is consolation and a promise of protection and aid, not a command to suppress natural fear, which lies outside choice.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد منه النهي عن الخوف لأنه من حيث كونه أمرا طبيعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear leaves human nature through God's creative command, as when He made the fire cool and safe for Abraham.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن الخوف إنما يزول عن جبلة الإنسان بأمر التكوين كما قال

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawī couplet presents reassurance as nourishment for the fearful: those who fear are made safe, while the person without fear does not need the lesson not to fear.
rows.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : لا تخافوا هست نزل خائفان هست درخور

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: I am with you means complete protection and victory, not spatial proximity, since God is transcendent beyond physical location.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ في "حواشيه" : ليس المراد منه النهي عن الخوف

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: God hears and sees what happens between them and Pharaoh, and acts to repel harm and bring benefit; one accompanied by God is protected from every tyrant.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ في "حواشيه" : ليس المراد منه النهي عن الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A young preacher imprisoned by al-Rashīd in a sealed room later appeared in a garden; he said the one who put him there had also brought him out, and the caliph wept and honored him.
rows.anchor: روي أن شابا كان يأمر وينهى فحبسه الرشيد في بيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coming to Pharaoh is not redundant with the prior command to go: coming implies easy arrival, whereas coming more generally considers reaching; either can describe intending to arrive.
rows.anchor: {فأتياه} أمرا بإتيانه الذي هو عبارة عن الوصول إليه بعدما أمرا بالذهاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are to state their message from the outset so the tyrant understands their claim and frames his reply accordingly.
rows.anchor: {فقولا} من أول الأمر {إنا رسولا ربك} ليعرف الطاغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rasūl is the dual of rasūl, a rare faʿūl form meaning one who bears a message; conventionally it can be human or angel sent to convey rulings, while nabī is restricted to a human.
rows.anchor: ورسولا تثنية رسول وهو فعول مبالغة مفعل بضم الميم وفتح العين

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr explains the request as releasing the Israelites and letting them go with Moses and Aaron to Palestine, their ancestral home; Palestine lies between Syria and Egypt and includes Ramla, Gaza, and Ascalon.
rows.anchor: ما قال في "بحر العلوم" فأطلقهم وخلهم يذهبوا معنا إلى فلسطين

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshād takes sending to mean freeing the Israelites from captivity and oppressive control, not requiring them to travel to Syria; the prohibition on torment supports this reading.
rows.anchor: وقال في "الإرشاد" بالإرسال إطلاقهم من الأسر والقسر وإخراجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites were subjected to hard labor such as digging and carrying stones, their sons were killed every other year, and their women were made servants.
rows.anchor: فإنهم كانوا تحت مملكة القبط يستخدمونهم في الأعمال الصعبة الفادحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing the demand to release believers between the claim of messengership and the promised sign stresses that rescuing believers from unbelievers matters more than merely inviting them to faith.
rows.anchor: وتوسيط حكم الإرسال بين رسالتهما وبين ذكر المجيء بآية دالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdhāb means severe pain or affliction. Its proposed origins include making someone hungry and sleepless, removing life's sweetness, or repeatedly striking with the tip of a whip.
rows.anchor: والعذاب هو الإيجاء الشديد وقد عذبه تعذيبا أي : أكثر حبسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign is singular despite multiple miracles because the point is to establish their claim with proof, not enumerate the proofs.
rows.anchor: وتوحيد الآية مع تعددها لأن المراد إثبات الدعوى ببرهانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-salām identifies peace as a general kind; the expression can be read as a greeting whose implied blessing brings safety in both abodes.
rows.anchor: {والسلام} اللام لتعريف الماهية والسلامة التعري من الآفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-salām means safety and ʿalā functions like li, as in the reverse prepositional usage in the statement that they have the curse.
rows.anchor: وأما السلامة فعلى بمعنى اللام كعكسه في قوله تعالى : {ولهم اللعنة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following guidance means affirming God's truth-guiding signs, whether physically or by conforming and obeying; the latter sense also appears in the verse promising no fear to those who follow God's guidance.
rows.anchor: بتصديق آيات الله الهادية إلى الحق فاللام على أصلها كما في سلام عليكم

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt says whoever submits and follows God's guidance brought by His prophets is safe.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات" : سلم من استسلم واتبع هدى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḥy originally means a swift sign or communication; it may be secret speech through Gabriel, inspiration, or a dream.
rows.anchor: وأصل الوحي الإشارة السريعة وذلك قد يكون بالكلام الخفي على لسان جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses received revelation through Gabriel, while Aaron received it through Gabriel and through Moses.
rows.anchor: والوحي إلى موسى بوساطة جبريل وإلى هارون بوساطته ووساطة موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning means all punishment, worldly and everlasting in the next life, corresponding to all peace; finite punishment is negligible beside everlasting punishment.
rows.anchor: أي : كل العذاب لأنه في مقابله السلام أي : كل السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers reject God's signs and disbelieve what the prophets brought; lying applies to both speech and action.
rows.anchor: على من كذب} بآياته تعالى وكفر بما جاء به الأنبياء عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When used transitively or with an understood ʿan, tawallā means turning away and abandoning closeness by refusing the signs and following desire; the warning conveys its threat gently.
rows.anchor: {وتولى} إذا عدي بعن لفظا أو تقديرا اقتضى معنى الإعراض

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kāshifī narrates that Moses and Aaron came before Pharaoh by God's command, identified themselves as messengers and called him to worship God; Pharaoh then asked who their Lord was.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (س موسى وهارون بحكم حضرت الهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man is interrogative here, meaning who.
rows.anchor: {فمن} استفهامية : والمعنى بالفارسية

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the question as following from their claim to be messengers: if so, they must identify the Lord who sent them; Pharaoh's arrogance explains why he does not ask who his own Lord is.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره الفاء لترتيب السؤال على ما سبق من كونهما رسولي ربهما

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam links Pharaoh's question to his earlier boast that he raised Moses as a child: Pharaoh treats himself as Moses' lord and asks why Moses calls him to another Lord.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أثبت نفسه ربا في قوله : {ألم نربك فينا وليدا}

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Pharaoh addresses both brothers, then singles out Moses because he is the principal messenger and Aaron his minister and follower.
rows.anchor: خاطبهما ثم أفرد موسى إذ كان يعلم أن موسى هو الأصل في الباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the sky might seem preferable as the abode of elevated spirits, earth is favored because bodily instruments from the earthly realm make ascent possible; prayer's bodily form is worldly though heart and orientation are heavenly.
rows.anchor: كان الظاهر أن تفضل السماء لكونها مقر الأرواح العالية ولذا يبقى الجسد هنا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying three things of this world were beloved to him: perfume, women, and the delight of his eye in prayer.
rows.anchor: جعل عليه السلام الصلاة من الدنيا في قوله : "حبيب إلي من دنياكم ثلاث : الطيب ، والنساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite form of signs refers to the known signs, while kulluhā confirms that every kind was included.
rows.anchor: إضافة الآيات عهدية وكلها تأكيد لشمول الأنواع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through Moses God showed Pharaoh all the signs, including the staff and the hand, over time; alternatively He made their truth known and clarified their evidentiary force.
rows.anchor: أي : وبالله لقد بصرنا فرعون على يدي موسى آياتنا كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh denied all the signs from obstinacy, without pause or hesitation, and claimed they were magic.
rows.anchor: {فكذب} بالآيات كلها من فرط عناده من غير تردد وتأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibāʾ is intense refusal: every case of ibāʾ is refusal, but not every refusal is ibāʾ.
rows.anchor: والاباء شدة الامتناع فكل اباء امتناع وليس كل امتناع إباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is in your right hand means the staff; the deliberately unspecified wording magnifies it and signals that its extraordinary effects distinguish it from ordinary staffs.
rows.anchor: {وألق ما في يمينك} أي : عصاك والإبهام لتفخيم شأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talqaf is jussive as the response to the imperative.
rows.anchor: {تلقف ما صنعوا} بالجزم جواب للأمر من لقفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means to gulp or swallow quickly; al-Mufradāt says it can mean taking something by pulling, whether with the mouth or hand.
rows.anchor: قال في "المفردات" : لقفت الشيء القفه وتلقفته تناولته بالجذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is feminine because mā here stands for the staff.
rows.anchor: والتأنيث لكون ما عبارة عن العصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣunʿ is doing something skillfully: every craft is an act, but not every act is craft, and craft is not attributed to animals or inanimate things as general action is.
rows.anchor: والصنع إجادة الفعل فكل صنع فعل وليس كل فعل صنعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff will swallow ropes and sticks whose apparent motion and lightness frightened Moses; calling them what the magicians made belittles their work as deceit.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عنها بما صنعوا للتحقير والإيذان بالتمويه والتزوير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā can be a relative pronoun or an indefinite description, yielding either what they made or something they made.
rows.anchor: ما موصولة أو موصوفة أي : إن الذي صنعوه أو إن شيئا صنعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayd sāḥir is nominative as the predicate of inna; its indefinite form in an annexation belittles the sorcerer's kind of scheme.
rows.anchor: بالرفع على أنه خبر لأن أي : كيد جنس الساحر ومكره وحيلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A scheme can be praiseworthy or blameworthy, although the word is more commonly used for blameworthy plotting; the same usage tendency applies to istidrāj and makr.
rows.anchor: والكيد ضرب من الاحتيال يكون محمودا أو مذموما وإن كان يستعمل في المذموم أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magicians as a class never attain their aim wherever they practice magic; this completes the reason the staff defeats their work.
rows.anchor: {ولا يفلح الساحر} أي : لا يدرك بغيته هذا الجنس

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reads the staff as God's own making and scheme, while the magicians' work is theirs; their craft cannot prosper against His firm design.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن ما في يمينك هو مصنوعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly success means survival, wealth, power, and honor; afterlife success means permanence without death, wealth without poverty, honor without humiliation, and knowledge without ignorance. Worldly success alone ends in loss.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الفلاح دنيوي وهو الظفر بالسعادات التي تطيب بها حياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī illustrates the claim with a student who objects to his teacher and later prospers materially but remains a loser; he applies the lesson to wrongdoers and opponents.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى أن من قال لأستاذه لم أي : اعترض عليه لن يفلح أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa is explanatory: after the staff swallowed the objects and events unfolded, the magicians were thrown down prostrate.
rows.anchor: {فألقى السحرة} الفاء فصيحة أي : فإلقاه فوقع ما وقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their falling is called being cast, as if someone hurled them, matching the earlier casting of their implements and emphasizing the force of their fall.
rows.anchor: حال كونهم {سجدا} ساجدين كأنما ألقاهم ملقي لشدة خرورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian narrative says Moses' staff became a serpent and swallowed the tools; the crowd fled, Moses caught it and it reverted, and the magicians recognized a miracle rather than magic and sincerely prostrated.
rows.anchor: مردم ازترس روى بكريز آوردند وموسى اورا بكرفت همان عصا شد

rows.speaker: رئيسهم
rows.claim: The chief magician reasoned that their tools had always remained after they beat people; if Moses' feat were magic, their tools should still be there. Their disappearance showed a creator and confirmed Moses' mission, so they repented and prostrated.
rows.anchor: روي أن رئيسهم قال : كنا نغلب الناس وكانت الآلات تبقى علينا

rows.speaker: جار الله
rows.claim: Jār Allāh marvels at the contrast: they cast their ropes for disbelief, then cast down their heads in gratitude and prostration.
rows.anchor: قال جار الله : ما أعجب أمرهم القوا حبالهم للكفر والجحود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb قالوا is an explanatory resumption specifying what they said while prostrating.
rows.anchor: {قالوا} في سجودهم وهو استئناف بياني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mention Aaron before Moses to keep the rhyme and avoid mistaking Moses for Pharaoh, who raised him, if Moses were named alone or first; Aaron is secondary in the phrasing.
rows.anchor: تأخير موسى عند حكاية كلامهم لرعاية الفواصل ولأن فرعون ربى موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding their Lord to the two messengers means He is the one they call to and the one who performed the extraordinary acts through them.
rows.anchor: ومعنى إضافة الرب إليهما أنه هو الذي يدعوان إليه وأجرى على يديهما

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: A Sufi authority says devotion to God frees the heart from ego's claims, brings sincerity, certainty and divine lights; the magicians were drawn to God and believed by proof rather than imitation, while Pharaoh saw no proof of lordship.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : من كان له استعداد النظر إلى عالم الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh rebukes the magicians for believing Moses without his leave.
rows.anchor: {قال} فرعون للسحرة بطريق التوبيخ {له قبل} أي : لموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in له incorporates the sense of following into the verb.
rows.anchor: واللام لتضمين الفعل معنى الاتباع واللام مع الإيمان في كتاب الله

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr instead takes له to mean their Lord, with the lām functioning like bi; the parallel wording in al-Aʿrāf supports this reading.
rows.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" : له أي : لربهما على أن اللام بمعنى الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form read with a long vowel is declarative, expressing Pharaoh's reproach that they acted before he gave permission.
rows.anchor: وآمنتم بالمد على الاخبار أي : فعلتم هذا الفعل توبيخا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before means they acted without his permission; it does not imply permission was later given or expected. Permission is informing someone that an action is approved.
rows.anchor: من غير أن آذن لكم في الإيمان له وأمركم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh calls Moses the leading expert in their art and their teacher.
rows.anchor: {إنه} يعني موسى {لكبيركم} أي : في فنكم وأعلمكم به

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kāshifī glosses Pharaoh's charge as calling Moses the magicians' master, teacher, and senior.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (يعني استاد ومعلم ومهتر جادوانست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh fabricates a conspiracy to keep his people from following the magicians; he pretends faith requires his leave, so their unauthorized conversion is invalid, although he knows Moses did not teach them magic.
rows.anchor: وأراد التلبيس على قومه لئلا يتبعوا السحرة في الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat implies an oath, and the intensive verb form signals repeated cutting; the same intensification applies to the following threat. Cutting can refer to perceptible bodies or intelligible things.
rows.anchor: {فلاقطعن} أي : فوالله لأقطعن وصيغة التفعيل للتكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khilāf is broader than opposition: every pair of opposites differs, but not every pair that differs is opposite.
rows.anchor: الخلاف أعم من الضد لأن كل ضدين مختلفان دون العكس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat means cutting one limb from each side, such as the right hand and left foot; min marks the starting point from opposite rather than matching limbs, and the phrase describes their dissimilar state.
rows.anchor: والمعنى من كل شق طرفا وهو أن يقطع اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specific crosswise amputation makes the punishment more dreadful than other forms and strengthens the threat.
rows.anchor: وتعيين القطع وكيفيته لكونه أفظع من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Crucifixion means fastening a person's back to wood, here palm trunks along the Nile.
rows.anchor: الصلب الذي هو تعليق الإنسان للقتل قيل هو شد صلبه على خشب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using in with the palm trunks suggests the magicians will remain there a long time, like an object settled inside its container.
rows.anchor: وإيثار كلمة في للدلالة على إبقائهم عليها زمانا طويلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Pharaoh was the first to employ crucifixion.
rows.anchor: قالوا : فرعون موسى هو أول من استعمل الصلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the recent miracle might make such threats seem implausible, Pharaoh may be deeply frightened yet feign toughness to maintain his public authority.
rows.anchor: قلنا : يجوز أن يكون في أشد الخوف ويظهر الجلادة تمشية لناموسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh means that the magicians will learn whether he or Moses is harsher and more enduring in punishment; Moses had inflicted no punishment, but Pharaoh thought they feared for their lives after seeing the staff swallow their tools.
rows.anchor: {ولتعلمن أينآ} أي : أنا وموسى

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Under al-Baḥr's earlier reading of له as their Lord, the comparison is between Pharaoh himself and the Lord of Moses.
rows.anchor: وعلى ما سبق من "بحر العلوم" في {له قبل}

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says Pharaoh speaks of severe punishment because he knows worldly pain but is blind to the severity of punishment in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : وإنما قال : {أشد عذابا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umm can mean one's immediate or ancestral mother, or more broadly any origin, source, upbringing, repair, or beginning of something.
rows.anchor: الأم بازاء الأب وهي الوالدة القريبة التي ولدته والبعيدة التي ولدت من ولدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original form is yā ibn ummī; the yāʾ changes to alif and is then dropped, retaining the fatḥa because the expression is frequent and lengthy and the doubled consonant is heavy.
rows.anchor: وأصله يا ابن أمي أبدل الياء ألفا فقيل : يا ابن أما ثم حذف الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has yā ibn umm with the final yāʾ omitted and its kasra retained.
rows.anchor: وقرىء يا ابن أم بالكسر بحذف الياء والاكتفاء بالكسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling him son of my mother honors the mother, softens Aaron's heart, invokes their kinship, and signals that they shared a womb.
rows.anchor: وخص الأم بالإضافة استعظاما لحقها وترقيقا لقلبه واعتدادا لنسبها

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority hold that Moses and Aaron had both the same father and mother.
rows.anchor: وإلا فالجمهور عل أنهما لأب وأم

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some Sufi masters say Aaron's prophethood came from the presence of mercy, and Moses calls him son of his mother because mercy and nurturing are associated with mothers.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار كانت نبوة هارون من حضرة الرحمة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya portrays Moses returning from the divine presence overwhelmed by longing and intimacy, while Aaron humbles himself to soften him through their maternal bond and recall the Sinai encounter when Moses fainted after asking to see God.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : لما رأى هارون موسى رجع من تلك الحضرة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The same esoteric account says Aaron's appeal recalls Moses fainting at the mountain and angels dragging his head while reproaching the mismatch between dust and the Lord of Lords.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : لما رأى هارون موسى رجع من تلك الحضرة

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafez's Persian verses picture the Simurgh's lofty nest as beyond ordinary hunters and their weak traps, extending the image of an inaccessible exalted station.
rows.anchor: قال الحافظ : برو اين دام برمرغ دكرنه كه عنقارا بلنداست آشيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses seized Aaron's head hair with his right hand and beard with his left in intense anger; seeing the calf worship, he could not restrain himself and acted before the people.
rows.anchor: روي أنه أخذ شعر رأسه بيمينه ولحيته بشماله من شدة غيظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron feared that if he fought some Israelites against others, Moses would accuse him of dividing the people; fighting could cause a separation from which they would never reunite.
rows.anchor: إنى خشيت} لو قاتلت بعضهم ببعض وتفرقوا {أن تقول فرقت
